newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia pledges tax-free terms for Sakhalin oil.
newsitem.headline: Russia pledges tax-free terms for Sakhalin oil.

text.p: Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Monday that Japanese companies will be guaranteed the tax-free conditions Moscow promised them last year for their Russian Far East oil projects.

"Now we organise tax-free conditions for Japanese companies who take part in Sakhalin 1 and Sakhalin 2," Nemtsov told Reuters, referring to the $22 billion worth of international oil and gas projects in the Sakhalin Island region north of Japan.
Nemtsov is in Tokyo this week as part of an 80-strong delegation aimed at courting new Japanese investment and boosting economic ties between the countries.

Sakhalin has two major production-sharing deals in initial stages: the $12 billion Sakhalin-I and the $10 billion Sakhalin II projects. The former, whose three deposits are said to boast reserves of some 2.5 billion barrels of crude oil and over 15 trillion cubic feet of natural gas, is expected to begin production around 2001 to 2002.

The Japanese presence in the area is spearheaded by the Sakhalin Oil and Gas Development Co Ltd, a group comprising the semi-governmental Japan National Oil Company and 13 other private Japanese firms.
